key_insight: A pretrained neural optimization layer enables solver-free decision-focused learning for NP-hard edge-selection problems without optimal-solution labels.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a quality–efficiency trade-off for routing decisions by reducing training cost and avoiding NP-hard solver calls at deployment.
method: Pretrain a neural optimization layer using objectives and constraint penalties, with graph-informed edge scoring and iterative refinement.
Freeze the layer and train a predictor through continuous decisions using a task-specific loss evaluated under observed parameters.
Deploy the predictor, optimization layer, and lightweight decoder to produce discrete decisions.
evidence_signal: On asymmetric traveling salesperson and endpoint-free orienteering tasks, the framework outperformed prediction-focused learning and most evaluated decision-focused baselines, with lower training time and faster deployment than solver-based approaches.
watch_item: Constraint penalties and lightweight decoding do not establish a general feasibility or optimality guarantee; validate decoded decisions under deployment conditions.
paper_title: Solver-Free Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Edge Selection
